title: Revolut Launch Takes on Big Four, Gets Deposit Taking Licence
body:
A new contender for the Accounts Leaderboard.
Key Points
APRA granted Revolut a full Authorised Deposit-taking Institution (ADI) licence, its first banking licence in the APAC region, meaning it can now legally take deposits from Australian customers rather than just offer its existing app-based services.
New savings accounts pay up to 5.05% p.a., with interest calculated and paid daily (not monthly), no minimum deposit or balance targets, and deposits protected up to $250,000 under the Financial Claims Scheme.
Licence conditions include a commitment to invest ~$400 million over five years and grow the ~120-person Australian workforce by about 20% within 18 months; revenue comes from subscription tiers rather than traditional fees, topping out at a $100/month "Ultra" plan.
Summary
APRA has granted Revolut an ADI banking licence, letting the UK-founded fintech (1M+ Australian users, 75M+ globally) take deposits in Australia for the first time since launching there six years ago. It now offers instant-access savings accounts at up to 5.05% p.a., interest paid daily, with no minimum deposits, growth targets, or withdrawal penalties, and government-backed protection up to $250,000.
It's also expanding its credit card offering: a $0 annual fee card with rewards across 44 airlines and retail gift cards (Uber, Woolworths, Big W). Existing app users will be auto-migrated to the new bank entity. Revenue comes from subscription tiers up to $100/month rather than conventional banking fees.
As a condition of the licence, Revolut committed to invest roughly $400 million over five years and grow its ~120-person local headcount by 20% within 18 months. This is Revolut's first APAC banking licence, following a similar UK licence earlier this year, alongside a push into the US market. The company, backed by Nvidia and SoftBank, is reportedly targeting an IPO in 2027 or 2028 at a valuation near US$200 billion.
